meta.subject: Information and Communication Technology
meta.chapterTitle: Types and components of computer systems
meta.title: Desktop vs laptop computers

topics.laptop-for-monitoring: Using laptops for control and monitoring

objectives: Describe what a desktop computer is and what a laptop computer is
Give advantages and disadvantages of desktops compared with laptops
Describe the design features of a laptop and why each is needed
Give typical uses of desktop and laptop computers

learn.title: What is a desktop computer?
learn.body: A traditional **desktop computer** is a general-purpose computer built from **separate parts**: a monitor, a keyboard, a mouse and a processor unit (often called the 'tower'). Because the parts are separate and joined by cables, a desktop usually stays in **one place**.

learn.title: What is a laptop computer?
learn.body: A **laptop** (also called a **notebook**) has the screen, keyboard, pointing device (touchpad) and processor **all in one unit**. This makes it very **portable** — you can close it and carry it anywhere.

learn.alt: A desktop computer with separate monitor, keyboard, mouse and tower next to an open laptop
learn.caption: Desktop: separate parts. Laptop: everything in one unit.
learn.imagePrompt: Clean flat illustration on a white background: on the left a desktop computer with a separate monitor, keyboard, mouse and tower unit joined by cables; on the right an open laptop. Friendly educational style, soft teal and amber colours, no text, no logos, no brand names.

learn.title: Three design features of a laptop
items: **Lightweight** — so it is easy to carry
**Low power consumption** — so the battery lasts longer
**Low heat output** — because there is little space inside for cooling

learn.title: Desktop vs laptop at a glance

rows.label: Portability
rows.b: Can be used almost anywhere, e.g. a café

rows.label: Upgrading
rows.a: Easier and cheaper; parts are standard
rows.b: Not always possible, e.g. adding more RAM

rows.label: Value
rows.a: Usually a better specification (e.g. faster processor) for the same price
rows.b: Less performance for the money, because parts must be small

rows.label: Power
rows.a: Plugs into the mains; power use is not critical
rows.b: Runs on a battery with limited life

rows.label: Heat
rows.a: Large case lets heat escape easily
rows.b: Small case, so cooling is a challenge

rows.label: Internet
rows.a: More likely to be wired, so the connection is steadier
rows.b: Usually Wi-Fi, so the speed can vary

rows.label: Risk
rows.a: Less likely to be stolen or damaged
rows.b: Easier to steal, drop or damage

rows.label: Desk space
rows.b: Only one cord; takes little space

learn.title: What are they used for?
items: **Both:** office work (word processing, spreadsheets, databases), education, games, and entertainment such as streaming TV
**Laptops also:** control and monitoring away from a desk, because they can run on their own battery

learn.body: A heating engineer visits a customer's home to service a gas boiler. She takes a laptop, connects it to the boiler and records how well it is working. Carrying a desktop to the boiler would not be practical — it has separate parts and needs a mains socket.

learn.title: Working in two places
learn.body: If you use a desktop at home and want to keep working at school, you need to move your files, for example on a **memory stick** or through **cloud storage**. Cloud storage helps, but some organisations do not allow **sensitive files** to be stored on the cloud. With a laptop, your files simply go with you.

learn.title: Be specific
learn.body: One-word answers like 'cheaper' or 'faster' often get no mark. Say what is cheaper or faster: 'spare parts are standard, so repairs cost less'.

learn.title: Comparing? Say both sides
learn.body: In a compare question, write each difference with both sides: 'A desktop is made of separate parts **whereas** a laptop is one single unit.'
Read which way the question asks! 'Advantages of a desktop compared with a laptop' — don't write 'it is portable'. That is a laptop advantage.

Some modern desktops are 'all-in-one' (the computer is built into the screen), and both desktops and laptops can use either a cable or Wi-Fi. For the exam, use the textbook's comparison: a traditional desktop with separate parts versus a laptop.

check.prompt: Which description best fits a traditional desktop computer?
check.hint: Picture a desktop computer on a school desk. Is it one single unit, or made of separate parts?
options: All parts are built into one single unit
It has a separate monitor, keyboard, mouse and processor unit
It always runs on an internal battery
It can only be controlled using a touch screen
check.explanation: Desktops are made of separate parts joined by cables. 'All parts in one unit' describes a laptop.

check.prompt: Tick (✓) whether each statement is true or false.
check.hint: Compare how the machines are powered, connected, carried and repaired; then decide whether each claim matches their usual design.

rows.statement: Desktops are usually easier and cheaper to upgrade than laptops.
rows.explanation: Desktop parts are standard and easy to reach.

rows.statement: Laptops usually have a steadier internet connection than desktops.
rows.explanation: Desktops are more likely to be wired, so their connection is steadier.

rows.statement: A laptop is easier to steal than a desktop.
rows.explanation: Laptops are small and portable, so they are easier to steal.

rows.statement: Power use is critical for a desktop because it runs on a battery.
rows.explanation: Desktops plug into the mains, so power use is not critical.

check.prompt: Tick (✓) whether each statement describes a desktop or a laptop.
check.hint: Use clues about mobility, replaceable components, cables and performance for the money to identify the better fit.

rows.statement: Only needs one cord, so there are fewer trailing wires
rows.explanation: Everything is in one unit, so a laptop needs just one cord.

rows.statement: Spare parts and connections are usually standard
rows.explanation: Standard parts make desktops cheaper to repair and upgrade.

rows.statement: Can easily be used in a café
Usually has a faster processor for the same price
rows.explanation: Desktops give a better specification for the money.

check.prompt: Complete each sentence using the most appropriate word from the list. Each word may be used once only.
check.hint: Recall how small computers manage cooling, how a fixed workstation may connect online, and whether hardware changes are always possible.

items.sentence: Laptops are designed to have a low ___ output because cooling is difficult in a small case.
Desktops are more likely to use a ___ internet connection, so the connection is steadier.
It is not always possible to ___ a laptop, for example by adding more RAM.

practice.prompt: Give two advantages of using a desktop computer rather than a laptop computer.

markPoints.point: Spare parts/connections are standardised / so repairs cost less
Easier / cheaper to upgrade or expand
Better specification / faster processor for the same price
Power use is not critical / uses mains electricity
Larger case gives better heat dissipation / cooling
Less likely to be stolen / damaged as it stays in one place
Steadier / more stable internet connection as usually wired

practice.modelAnswer: Spare parts are standard, so repairs cost less. It is usually wired, so its internet connection is steadier.
practice.explanation: Any two different valid points. Make each one specific — 'cheaper' alone is too vague.

practice.prompt: Give two disadvantages of laptop computers compared with desktop computers.

markPoints.point: Easier to steal
Limited battery life / may need to carry a heavy power adaptor
Keyboard / pointing device can be awkward to use
Not always possible to upgrade (e.g. add RAM)
Lower specification for the same price
Wi-Fi connection / data rate can vary
Harder / more expensive to repair

practice.modelAnswer: Laptops are easier to steal. The battery has limited life, so the user may need to carry a power adaptor.

practice.prompt: State three design features of a laptop computer that help to make it portable.

markPoints.point: Lightweight
Low power consumption / long battery life / energy efficient
Low heat output

practice.modelAnswer: Lightweight. Low power consumption. Low heat output.
practice.explanation: The three design features are lightweight, low power consumption and low heat output.

practice.prompt: Describe two design features of a laptop computer and why each one is needed.

markPoints.point: Lightweight
…so it is easy to carry / helps portability
Low power consumption
…so the battery lasts longer
Low heat output
…because cooling is difficult in a small case / to avoid overheating

practice.modelAnswer: A laptop is lightweight. This makes it easy to carry around. It has low power consumption. This makes the battery last longer.
practice.explanation: Describe = feature (1 mark) + why it is needed (1 mark), for two features. A reason only counts if you named its feature.

practice.prompt: Omar does his school projects both at school and at home. Explain why a laptop may be more suitable for Omar than a desktop computer.

markPoints.point: Laptop is portable / he can carry it between school and home
All parts are in one unit / nothing to disconnect and set up again
His files stay on the laptop / no need to copy files to a memory stick
Does not depend on cloud storage, which may not allow some files
Battery means he can work where there is no socket, e.g. while travelling

practice.modelAnswer: A laptop is portable, so Omar can carry it between school and home. His project files stay on the laptop, so he does not need to copy them onto a memory stick. It runs on its battery, so he can work while travelling.
practice.explanation: Explain = a point AND how it helps Omar (school and home). General facts not linked to Omar are weaker.

practice.prompt: Compare desktop and laptop computers. Your answer must include similarities and differences.

markPoints.point: Both are used for office work / education / games / entertainment
Both have a processor, keyboard, screen and pointing device
Desktop has separate parts whereas a laptop is a single unit
Laptop is portable whereas a desktop stays in one place
Desktop is easier / cheaper to upgrade than a laptop
Desktop has a better specification for the same price
Laptop runs on a battery whereas a desktop uses the mains
Desktop usually wired / steadier whereas laptop usually Wi-Fi / variable
Laptop is easier to steal / damage than a desktop

practice.modelAnswer: Both are used for office work and education. A desktop has separate parts whereas a laptop is one single unit. A laptop is portable whereas a desktop stays in one place. A desktop is easier to upgrade than a laptop.
practice.explanation: This question says you MUST include similarities and differences, so with differences only the most you can get is 3 out of 4. Write each difference with both sides, using 'whereas'.

practice.prompt: A heating engineer visits customers' homes to check how well their gas boilers are working. Explain why a laptop is more suitable than a desktop computer for this job.

markPoints.point: Laptop can be carried to the boiler / used at the customer's home
Runs on its own battery / no mains socket needed
Can be connected to the boiler to record / monitor its performance directly

practice.modelAnswer: The laptop can be carried to the customer's boiler. It runs on its battery, so it can be connected to the boiler to monitor how it is working.
practice.explanation: This is the 'control and monitoring' use of laptops — link your points to the engineer visiting homes.

summary: Desktop = separate parts, stays in one place. Laptop = everything in one unit, portable.
Desktop wins on: standard parts, upgrading, value for money, power, cooling, steadier wired internet, security.
Laptop wins on: portability, one cord, small desk space, Wi-Fi in different places.
Laptop design features: lightweight, low power consumption, low heat output.
Both: office work, education, gaming, entertainment. Laptops also: monitoring on site.
